newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX oil seen up on technicals, short-covering.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX oil seen up on technicals, short-covering.

text.p: NYMEX oil prices were called up Monday morning, bouncing off technical support following four consecutive sessions of declines while some dealers took the opportunity to cover short positions, traders said.
"Some of it is technical. Some of it is short-covering," said Refco Inc vice president Victor Yu.
Crude was called up 15 to 20 cents a barrel higher. Heating oil was called 0.50 to 0.75 cent a gallon higher while gasoline was called up 0.25 to 0.50 cent a gallon.
"Crude just got crushed last week, especially the March/ April spread, so there is a bounce now, but people are saying it's just a short-lived rally," said a New York crude dealer.
The March/April spread settled at 16 cents on Friday, falling from 41 cents last Monday.
"The open interest in March (crude) has come in a lot while it has expanded in April. The spread could come in further," said a dealer, noting March/April could slip into contango by week's end.

On Friday, March crude ended off 87 cents at $22.23 a barrel. March heat ended off 0.92 cent at 60.53 cents a gallon while March gasoline finished off 2.24 cents a gallon at 63.06 cents. Dealers noted support for crude at $22.25 on the spot continuation chart where crude gapped higher September 3.
Meanwhile, 60.00 cents was deemed key psychological support for March heating oil.
Dealers called the downtrend in oil prices seasonal, with the March month a period of relatively low demand for heating oil and gasoline.
In the news, two of Mexico's three crude ports, Pajaritos and Dos Bocas, were reopened after being shut due to bad weather over the weekend.
((-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761))
